matches.rationale: GT1 concerns overstating the linear relationship between categorization performance and neural alignment in the Abstract, requiring cross-section verification with later results. None of the findings address this claim interpretation issue or the relationship between performance and alignment.

GT2 identifies a fabricated citation (Grant, 2025) and overly specific behavioral claims about whiskers in hunting. No finding mentions this fabricated reference or the Introduction's behavioral claims.
GT3 concerns the inconsistency of describing a 5×7 array with zero padding for 30 whiskers in the Method section. None of the findings address this whisker array configuration issue.

GT4 identifies missing hyperparameter adjustment protocols for balancing two datasets with different simulation frequencies and augmentation counts. Finding 2 discusses inconsistencies in Table 1's sweep counts but does not address the lack of training protocol adjustments between datasets.

GT5 concerns selective reporting in the Experiments section that inflates effectiveness by emphasizing only top models. None of the findings address this selective reporting issue in the main Experiments section.

GT6 identifies overgeneralized rhetoric about tactile augmentations being critical and image augmentations causing training failure. No finding addresses this rhetorical manipulation in the Experiments section.
GT7 concerns the omission of ethical reflection on data scarcity limitations in the Discussion. None of the findings address this ethical integrity omission.

GT8 identifies an inconsistency where the ±1 N simulation clipping range is roughly one-tenth of maximal bite force (8-10 N), potentially contradicting biological plausibility claims. None of the findings address this force range justification issue.
GT9 concerns missing detailed hyperparameter reporting for SSL training stages in the Method section. None of the findings address this incomplete computational protocol reporting.
GT10 identifies implausible zero accuracies in Table 6 (Appendix) for stimulus decoding tasks. None of the findings mention Table 6 or these zero-accuracy anomalies.

GT11 concerns inconsistent equation numbering and undefined variables (y_t^ℓ) in the IntersectionRNN update equations in the Appendix. Finding 3 identifies that update rules are in Appendix A2 not A3, but does not address the equation inconsistencies themselves.

GT12 identifies cross-section inconsistency between Abstract claims of saturating explainable variance and Discussion acknowledgment of dataset limitations. None of the findings address this Abstract-Discussion inconsistency.
GT13 concerns speculative rhetoric in the Discussion about GPT-based attenders implying biological attention mechanisms. None of the findings address this rhetorical overextension.
GT14 identifies the omission of discussing biases from small sample size (11 mice, 999 units) in the Discussion. None of the findings address this ethical reporting omission.

GT15 concerns missing parameter count and compute budget balancing in comparisons between ConvRNN and other encoders in Experiments. None of the findings address this experimental design fairness issue.

GT16 identifies neural fit scores exceeding the maximum inter-animal consistency (1.34 vs 0.34), indicating potential overfitting or calculation errors. Finding 1 directly identifies the same issue: the impossible maximum of 1.34 for a metric bounded on [-1,1], noting it should be 0.34 based on Fig. 4b.

GT17 concerns fabricated claims in Related Work about providing the first neural comparison across 64 models, misrepresenting cited works that focus on visual cortex. None of the findings address this reference fabrication in Related Work.
